item.title: OpenTelemetry plugin enables comprehensive tracing and metrics for Hermes Agent
item.description:
OpenTelemetry plugin enables comprehensive tracing and metrics for Hermes Agent

An OpenTelemetry plugin has been released for Hermes Agent, enabling detailed observability for AI agent workflows. This update allows every interaction and process within the agent to be tracked and exported to compatible backends.

🔍 Overview

The plugin integrates Hermes Agent with OpenTelemetry (OTel) standards. It captures various operational aspects of the agent, including:

  • Model calls and API requests
  • Tool calls and skill loads
  • Approvals and delegated sub-agents

All of these events are structured into a single OTel trace for each Hermes turn. This trace includes metrics for tokens, costs, and latency. Optionally, logs and structured events are also captured and exported to any OTLP backend via HTTP or gRPC.

🧩 How it works

The plugin uses a comprehensive attribute schema to log details across different components of the agent. Attributes are emitted in two conventions to support various backends:

  • OpenInference (llm.*, input.value): Optimized for Phoenix.
  • OTel GenAI (gen_ai.*): Optimized for Langfuse, Weave, and generic dashboards.

This dual-convention approach eliminates the need for custom mapping in backend configurations.

⚙️ Key details

Specific trace data includes:

Component Tracked Details
Skills Name, source (skill_view / path read), path; remains open until the turn ends
Model Calls Model, provider, input user message, output assistant response
Metrics Token counts (incl. cache and reasoning buckets), duration, finish reason, request parameters
Errors ERROR status, exception details, and retry metadata
Tool Calls Arguments, results, inferred target/command, and hermes.tool.outcome (completed, error, timeout, blocked, cancelled)
Approvals Decision wait time, choice (once, session, always, deny, timeout, smart_approve, smart_deny, smart_escalate), and who decided
Sub-agents Role, goal, status, duration, summary, child’s model, and total subtree cost
Kanban A card’s run is traced from the dispatcher’s claim through the worker’s turn

The hermes.query_source attribute distinguishes the origin of calls:

  • main: The agent loop’s own calls
  • subagent: A delegated child’s calls
  • auxiliary: Calls made on the agent’s behalf (e.g., titling, compression, Mixture-of-Agents references, vision). These are tagged with hermes.auxiliary.task.

For successful git commit operations, the plugin records hermes.tool.git_commit, which is also counted as a hermes.commit.count and a commit event.

🚀 Multi-agent Support

The plugin supports complex orchestration patterns:

  • Delegated children
  • Kanban workers operating on different profiles and models
  • Swarms
  • Mixture-of-Agents
  • Cron jobs

In multi-agent runs, child executions are nested within the trace, ensuring that a single connected trace represents the entire workflow. GPU and CPU utilization are monitored using host metrics.

#OpenTelemetry #AIAgents #HermesAgent #Observability #LLMOps

Source: briancaffey/hermes-otel

item.title: Hermes Memory UI Released for Agent Inspection
item.description:
Hermes Memory UI Released for Agent Inspection

The Read-only Hermes Agent plugin has been introduced for inspecting memory in the Hermes Dashboard and Hermes Desktop, providing a unified Python backend API alongside separate delivery artifacts.

🔍 Overview

  • Read-only Hermes Agent plugin for inspecting memory in Hermes Dashboard and Hermes Desktop.
  • The Dashboard and Desktop interfaces are separate delivery artifacts sharing only the profile-aware Python backend API.
  • The plugin is intentionally read-only and does not add, edit, replace, or remove memories.
  • Writes must go through Hermes’ memory and fact_store tools or provider classes to preserve validation, locking, mirroring, FTS, HRR vectors, and memory-bank maintenance.

🧩 Supported Memory Sources

Memory Source Description / Capabilities
Built-in memory (MEMORY.md, USER.md) Agent notes, environment facts, project conventions, user profile, and preferences. Works always.
Session search Explicit read-only search over previous Hermes sessions via session_search tool, with optional source/type filters (CLI, Telegram, cron, Discord, web, API).
Holographic memory Local SQLite fact store at $HERMES_HOME/memory_store.db tracking facts, categories, trust scores, retrieval counters, and timestamps.
Mem0 memory Read-only Mem0 Platform memories via provider config, including scopes, scores, timestamps, and metadata.
Honcho memory Read-only Honcho workspace, host, peer, and provider configuration state with user/AI peer cards, representations, conclusions, and context search.
Mnemosyne memory Read-only local SQLite store inspection for episodes, facts, instructions, gists, and graph rows, with explicit recall and injected-context preview.
Hindsight memory Read-only/query-only Hindsight provider configuration state with explicit recall and reflect actions, and contents view for memory units and retained source documents.
ByteRover memory Read-only ByteRover CLI (brv) project status and registered locations, supporting explicit BM25 search and optional query/synthesis action.

⚙️ Key Technical Details

  • Built-in memory view works always, while external memory provider sections show only when configured.
  • Dashboard is a web plugin with its own manifest, tracked browser bundle, and stylesheet (dashboard/).
  • Desktop plugin (desktop/plugin.js) is a standalone, uncompiled ESM disk plugin importing only the Hermes Desktop SDK, React, and the JSX runtime without requiring an npm build.
  • The Desktop plugin registers the /memory full-page route, a Memory sidebar item, and an Open Memory command-palette action.
  • Desktop requests use the plugin-scoped, profile-aware ctx.rest client reaching the same /api/plugins/hermes-memory-ui/ backend used by Dashboard.
  • The regular plugin must be installed and present in plugins.enabled so Hermes mounts dashboard/plugin_api.py.

🚀 Installation and Availability

  • Default profile lives at ~/.hermes, while a named profile lives at ~/.hermes/profiles/<name> (use hermes -p <name> and set HERMES_HOME="$HOME/.hermes/profiles/<name>").
  • Install directly from GitHub: hermes plugins install xraysight/hermes-memory-ui --enable.
  • To enable the Hermes Desktop interface, copy the disk plugin to $HERMES_HOME/desktop-plugins/hermes-memory-ui/plugin.js.
  • Hermes Desktop inventories the UI separately under Settings → Plugins.
  • Update existing installation using hermes plugins update hermes-memory-ui.

#HermesAgent #AIPlugins #MemoryManagement #DeveloperTools

Source: xraysight/hermes-memory-ui

item.title: Turning a VPS into a 24/7 AI Worker with Hermes Agent or OpenClaw
item.description:
Turning a VPS into a 24/7 AI Worker with Hermes Agent or OpenClaw

A VPS can now be turned into an AI Worker by installing an AI Agent platform such as Hermes Agent or OpenClaw, connecting a language model, granting tools, and configuring a command channel.

🔍 Overview

  • AI Worker: an AI Agent deployed on a VPS that receives tasks, uses AI and authorized tools, and operates continuously 24/7.
  • The concept is supported by platforms like Hermes Agent and OpenClaw.
  • Communication can be routed through Telegram or Slack, allowing you to assign work from a phone.

🛠️ How to Build an AI Worker

The general workflow consists of six steps:

  1. Prepare VPS – provision a Linux VPS (commonly Ubuntu) with suitable CPU, RAM, and admin/SSH access.
  2. Install AI Agent – deploy an Agent platform such as Hermes Agent or OpenClaw.
  3. Connect Model – link the Agent to an external LLM via API key (e.g., GPT, Claude, Gemini, OpenRouter).
  4. Grant Tools – provide the Agent with the utilities it needs (browser, file handlers, custom scripts, Docker if required).
  5. Set Communication Channel – configure Telegram, Slack, or another webhook for inbound commands.
  6. Create Automation – define schedules, scripts, or pipelines the Agent will execute autonomously.

⚙️ Technical Requirements

  • Operating System: Linux (Ubuntu is typical).
  • Access: SSH or full administrative rights.
  • Model Access: API key for the chosen LLM service.
  • Docker: Needed only if the selected Agent or sandbox demands it.
  • Communication: Telegram or Slack bot/webhook for remote task submission.
  • Additional: Domain name and HTTPS if a web interface or external webhook is exposed.
  • Hardware: No GPU required when the Agent calls models via API; CPU and RAM support the Agent, browser, tools, and background services.

🤖 Capabilities

  • Receive requests from Telegram/Slack.
  • Process files, perform web searches, run shell commands.
  • Utilize Skills and Persistent Memory (Hermes Agent) to reuse experience across sessions.
  • Remember data between interactions and execute scheduled jobs.
  • Operate continuously without dependence on a personal computer’s power state.

📊 Platform Comparison

Platform Type Notable Features
Hermes Agent AI Agent Skills, Persistent Memory, learning loop, extensible memory providers (as described in official docs)
OpenClaw AI Agent General AI Agent example for deployment on a VPS

The practical capability of an AI Worker depends on the chosen Agent, the language model, and the granted tools.

#AIWorker #VPS #AIAgents #HermesAgent #OpenClaw

item.title: NVIDIA NeMo Relay Integration for Hermes Agent Observability
item.description:
NVIDIA NeMo Relay Integration for Hermes Agent Observability

The Hermes Agent harness now includes native integration with NVIDIA NeMo Relay, allowing developers to record and evaluate agent sessions, turns, model calls, and tool calls.

🧩 How it works

NeMo Relay records lifecycle events as work begins and ends, preserving timing and parent-child relationships. This integration utilizes several formats and standards for observability:

Format/Standard Description
Agent Trajectory Observability Format (ATOF) A JSONL log of scope starts, ends, and point-in-time marks with IDs and timestamps to reconstruct the agent run.
Agent Trajectory Interchange Format (ATIF) A step-by-step JSON record of agent interactions, tool calls, and observations assembled from lifecycle events.
OpenTelemetry with OpenInference Records the run as parent-child spans, using OpenInference to label agent, LLM, and tool spans and define their attributes.

⚙️ Key details

Users can run Hermes Agent examples using a self-contained environment (Python 3.11, Hermes 0.21.1, and NeMo Relay 0.8.3) created via a setup script in the nemoclaw-community repository.

Capabilities and constraints include:

  • Terminal Tool Sandbox: Hermes uses a terminal tool to run Python scripts inside an isolated Docker container that cannot access the network, repository checkout, or NVIDIA API key.
  • Host Security: Hermes cannot fall back to running terminal commands on the host.
  • Observability Tools: Users can explore OpenTelemetry traces in Arize Phoenix.
  • Evaluation: The Hermes ToolPerf case study demonstrates using this approach to evaluate harness changes across repeated runs by combining task verification with trace evidence.

🚀 Availability

To get started, the following prerequisites are required:

  • macOS or Linux
  • Git and curl
  • Docker Desktop or Docker Engine
  • An NVIDIA Build API key for NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning

#NVIDIA #NeMoRelay #HermesAgent #OpenTelemetry #AIAgents

Source: Tracing Agent Harness Behavior with NVIDIA NeMo Relay | NVIDIA Technical Blog
